README.md:182: * **Never:** task names, prompts, briefs, paths, thread ids, `consult_id`, finding texts, notes,
README.md:183:   topics, labels as typed, the coordinator's host, user names, keys. The server drops
README.md:184:   secret-named keys on arrival and reports how many; C3 treats a non-zero count as its own bug.
README.md:185: * **Off:** `CODEX_CONSULT_TELEMETRY=off` (any value other than unset/`on`/`1`/`true`/`yes`
README.md:186:   counts as off), or `--telemetry off` per run - a run's own `--telemetry on|off` wins over the
README.md:187:   variable, and a panel passes it to its members. The first run after an install prints this
README.md:188:   notice once; the dry run says whether it is on.
README.md:189: * **Never blocks a run; never lost silently:** events queue in C3's own outbox
README.md:190:   (`<codex home>/c3/telemetry/spool.ndjson`, one `{v, kind, queued_unix, body}` line each - not
README.md:191:   the plugin's `telemetry-spool/`: C3 is its own app with its own salt and instance id), are sent
README.md:192:   by a detached sender a run starts right after its commit (a consultation, a panel - once -, a
README.md:193:   rating, a backfill; the run never waits for it, and it gets an allow-listed environment only: no
README.md:194:   key, no host marker) in batches of at most 100 (one flush ends after 60 s, one request after 8 s),
README.md:195:   retried by the next sender and dropped 7 days after they were queued. The sender follows the
README.md:196:   intake's answers as the plugin does: a 429 whose `Retry-After` is at most 60 s is waited for
README.md:197:   once (else the batch stays queued), a 400 naming `events[i]` drops that event and resends the
README.md:198:   rest (at most three per flush), a 413 halves the batch and drops an event too large alone -
README.md:199:   each refused event is one line of the last flush's `rejected` - and a 403, another refusal or no
README.md:200:   answer stops the flush with the outbox kept. Appends and the sender are synchronised by a lock,
README.md:201:   and the sender removes only the lines it delivered or dropped - an event queued while it sends
README.md:202:   stays queued. The sender lock's owner record (`flush.owner.json`) lets `--status` and a refused
README.md:203:   sender say "sender busy since <t>", and after 30 minutes "sender stuck since <t> (pid <n>)". An event that cannot be
README.md:204:   spooled is said and counted (`c3 telemetry --status`); a rating's event is retried and else
README.md:205:   left for `c3 telemetry --backfill-ratings`.
README.md:206: * **Complaints:** `c3 --complain "<text>"` prints the exact payload (your text plus the last
README.md:207:   ledger entry's summary - classes only), asks before sending, and prints a public reference
README.md:208:   like `T-7KQ4-M2XZ` to quote on the forum section <https://xelth.com/F/p/c3> or in a mail.
README.md:209: * **Delete my data:** `c3 forget-me` (or `c3 telemetry --forget --public-ref <ref> [--local]`,
README.md:210:   or `DELETE https://xelth.com/T/v2/instances/<instance_id>?public_ref=<ref>`) asks the intake to
README.md:211:   remove every event and complaint this installation ever sent - proved by a complaint's public
README.md:212:   reference - and removes the local salt, outbox and references only AFTER the intake confirmed
README.md:213:   it. A DELETE the intake does not confirm deletes nothing locally: the instance id and the
README.md:214:   reference stay, the pending deletion is recorded (`forget-pending.json`) and nothing is
README.md:215:   spooled or sent until `c3 forget-me` retries it with the same identity and the intake
README.md:216:   confirms. Without any public reference the intake cannot verify ownership:
README.md:217:   `c3 forget-me --local` (or `c3 telemetry --forget --local`) removes the local data only, and
README.md:218:   says that the intake keeps what was sent.
README.md:219: * **`c3 telemetry`:** `--status` (the switch and its source, the intake, the outbox, the events
README.md:220:   not spooled since the last flush, the sender lock's owner, a pending deletion, the last flush,
README.md:221:   the instance id),
README.md:222:   `--flush`, `--forget`, `--backfill-ratings [--dry-run]`. The intake is
README.md:223:   `CODEX_CONSULT_TELEMETRY_URL` when set (https only; plain http only to a loopback host in test
README.md:224:   mode), else `https://xelth.com/T`.
